label: Every composite has at least two distinct components
paraphrase: Every composite x has two components a and b with a ≠ b. This is the weaker numerical-diversity consequence of the q.11 a.1 divided-parts reading: the Lean formula does not require a ≠ x or b ≠ x, hence does not by itself assert genuine proper parts. The stronger proper-part case is tested explicitly by the COMPOSITE-UNITING-CAUSE-CONTROLS finite interpretation. Stronger than STMT-COMPOSITE-HAS-COMPONENT-OTHER-THAN-ITSELF in the number of mutually distinct components, not by a proper-part predicate.
